fidelity: F2a — Physics-Lumped Stack Model (electrochemical + SOC + fade/crossover + thermal ODE)
description: 0D/1D physics-lumped aqueous organic redox flow battery (AORFB) stack. Nernst (organic redox couple + SOC) with Butler-Volmer activation, ohmic ASR, and SOC/flow-limited concentration overpotentials; Coulomb-counting SOC ODE; first-order capacity-fade/crossover (organic decomposition, CE<1); lumped thermal ODE via scipy.solve_ivp. Representative chemistry: AQDS/ferricyanide (Aziz group).
source: Huskinson et al. (2014) Nature 505, 195 (Aziz group); Lin et al. (2015) Science 349, 1529; Kwabi, Ji & Aziz (2020) Chem. Rev. 120, 6467; Bard & Faulkner (2001) Electrochemical Methods; Newman & Thomas-Alyea (2004) Electrochemical Systems; Tang et al. (2014) J. Power Sources 248

unit.name: Generic 20-cell organic RFB stack, 100 cm2 electrode area, 1 L tanks

N_cells.note: Cells in series in the stack

E0.note: Standard cell potential for AQDS/ferricyanide couple (~0.7 V); alkaline quinone variants reach 1.0-1.2 V. Huskinson 2014; Lin 2015.

R_cell_ohm_cm2_ref.note: Area-specific resistance (ASR) at T_ref. High-performance alkaline quinone cell ~0.88 Ohm.cm2 (Lin 2015 Science); engineered AORFB cells 0.5-1.5 Ohm.cm2. (F1 used a conservative 6 Ohm.cm2; the F2 operating model uses a realistic low-ASR stack.)

j0_A_cm2.note: Exchange current density at T_ref for the quinone couple (fast, reversible organic kinetics). Representative; Bard & Faulkner Butler-Volmer.

j_L_A_cm2.note: Mass-transport limiting current density at full SOC and reference flow; comfortably above the rated operating envelope (peak ~0.5 A/cm2). Scales with reactant availability (SOC) and flow_factor. Lin 2015 peak power demos; Newman & Thomas-Alyea 2004.

electrolyte_conc_M.note: Active-species molarity; organic RFBs are solubility-limited vs vanadium. Lin 2015 ran ~0.5-1.0 M.

tank_volume_L.note: Electrolyte tank volume per side; sets stored capacity Q_cap = n*F*C*V.

pump_loss_coefficient.note: Parasitic pump power P = k_pump*I^2 (Tang 2014 flow/pressure scaling).

coulombic_efficiency.note: CE<1: organic active species decompose (anthrone formation, Michael addition, dimerisation) and cross over the membrane; reported CE ~0.97-0.995 for AQDS/DHAQ systems. Kwabi, Ji & Aziz (2020) Chem. Rev. 120, 6467.
coulombic_efficiency.source: Kwabi, Ji & Aziz (2020); Huskinson et al. (2014)

flow_factor.note: Electrolyte flow multiplier on limiting current j_L; >1 for higher flow rate, improving mass transport. Tang et al. (2014).

E_a.note: Activation energy governing exchange current density and ASR temperature dependence (Arrhenius). Representative for organic RFB.
E_a.source: Huskinson et al. (2014); Kwabi et al. (2020)

dOCV_dT.note: Entropic temperature coefficient of standard potential for the quinone/ferricyanide couple (~-0.2 to -0.4 mV/K), dominated by proton-coupled electron transfer entropy.
dOCV_dT.source: Kwabi et al. (2020); Yang et al. (2011) ChemSusChem 4, 1338

m_cp.note: Lumped heat capacity of stack + circulating electrolyte (~2 L aqueous, cp~4180 J/kg/K, plus stack hardware).

hA.note: Overall heat-loss coefficient (h*A) from stack/tanks to ambient (natural convection).

k_fade_ref.note: First-order capacity fade rate at T_ref ~ 0.1 %/day, characteristic of AQDS. Engineered molecules (DHAQ, BTMAP-Vi) reach <0.01 %/day.

Ea_fade.note: Activation energy of organic decomposition; fade accelerates strongly with temperature (upper limit ~40 degC). Kwabi et al. (2020).
